title: Quantum mechanics
summary: In 1925 Werner Heisenberg invented matrix mechanics, the first version of quantum mechanics, and Max Born and Pascual Jordan at Göttingen recognized its algebra as matrix algebra. The three published a paper developing it in 1926. In 1927 Heisenberg proposed the uncertainty relation, which limits how precisely a particle's position and velocity can both be known, and attended the Solvay Conference in Brussels.

uncertainty.note: Spans from Planck's 1900 blackbody radiation quantum hypothesis to the formulation of matrix mechanics in 1925 and the landmark 1927 Fifth Solvay Conference in Brussels.

importance.justification: Quantum mechanics fundamentally replaced classical mechanics for microscopic systems, serving as the universal theoretical basis of atomic physics, modern chemistry, semiconductors, and nuclear energy.

related.because: Max Planck's 1900 derivation of the blackbody radiation law introduced energy quanta, initiating quantum theory.
